properties.name: Chiemsee
properties.source_feature_id: DEBYBDLMcW0003Vc; DEBYBDLMcX0003k0; DEBYBDLMdW00040m; DEBYBDLMdW00040n; DEBYBDLMdW00040t; DEBYBDLMdX00055B
properties.geometry_epoch: modern ATKIS Basis-DLM; open-water reference for circa 1900
properties.historical_evidence_note: Endrös (1906), p. 344 and plate II, describes a roughly 0.7 m lowering in 1902–1904 and compares the earlier and later shorelines. The lake basin predates the change. The southeastern bays and Tiroler Achen delta have especially changed.

properties.name: Thunersee
properties.geometry_epoch: modern swissTLMRegio 2026; open-water reference for circa 1900
properties.historical_evidence_note: The lake predates the Kander diversion of 1714. The two main outlet gates were in place by 1818. The Kander delta and present shoreline may differ from circa 1900, and the 2009 flood-relief tunnel came later.

properties.name: Lac de Neuchâtel
properties.geometry_epoch: modern swissTLMRegio 2026; open-water reference for circa 1900
properties.historical_evidence_note: The first Jura water correction lowered the lake by 2.7 m in 1868–1891. The second correction of 1962–1973 lowered it again by about 0.5 m. The basin and open water predate both works; circa-1900 shallow shores remain uncertain.

properties.name: Lake Inawashiro
properties.attribution: HydroLAKES (Messager et al. 2016), HydroSHEDS; two feature geometries selected and exported in WGS84
properties.geometry_epoch: modern HydroLAKES open-water reference for a lake documented before 1900
properties.historical_evidence_note: Japanese Ministry of the Interior works record documents withdrawal from the existing lake in the 1870s. Fukushima Prefecture documents the 1879 Jurokkyo control gate and its Taisho-era modernization. Geometry supplies a modern open-water reference; circa-1900 shore elevations have not been reconstructed.

properties.name: Lago Todos los Santos
properties.attribution: HydroLAKES (Messager et al. 2016), HydroSHEDS; two feature geometries selected and exported in WGS84
properties.geometry_epoch: modern HydroLAKES open-water reference for a lake documented before 1900
properties.historical_evidence_note: Hans Steffen mapped this natural lake in 1897 after 1892 and 1892–1893 field expeditions. The national cultural heritage service confirms the expeditions. The modern SWBD outline is an open-water reference and is not a georectified copy of the 1897 map.

properties.name: Erhai
properties.attribution: HydroLAKES (Messager et al. 2016), HydroSHEDS; feature geometries selected and exported in WGS84
properties.geometry_epoch: modern HydroLAKES open-water reference for a lake documented before 1900
properties.historical_evidence_note: Ming-era Dian Lue, volume 2, identifies Erhai east of Dali. The present outlet and levels are managed under the Yunnan provincial regulation; gauge-based lake-level research documents a roughly 3 m post-1974 decline to the early-1980s minimum. SWBD supplies a modern reference for the basin's persistent water. Circa-1900 shoreline differences, especially the north shore, are unresolved. Elevation reconstruction is outside this surface classification.

properties.name: Lago de Atitlán
properties.attribution: HydroLAKES (Messager et al. 2016), HydroSHEDS; feature geometries selected and exported in WGS84
properties.geometry_epoch: modern HydroLAKES open-water reference for a lake documented before 1900
properties.historical_evidence_note: Map 8 reproduces the 1894 Plan of the Ejidos of San Pedro La Laguna (Archivo General de Centroamérica, Sección de Tierras, Sololá, paquete 9, expediente 4) explicitly labeling Lago de Atitlán. AMSCLAE documents the natural endorheic lake and measured shoreline-level variation. SWBD supplies a modern reference for the open lake. The exact circa-1900 shoreline and level are unresolved.

properties.name: Atlin Lake / Áa Tlein
properties.attribution: HydroLAKES v1.0, Messager et al. (2016), CC BY 4.0. Geometry simplified to 35 m before conversion to WGS84.
properties.historical_record: Geological Survey of Canada field account, 1899, and the British Columbia mining map show the pre-existing lake.
properties.geometry_epoch: Modern HydroLAKES open water reference. Seasonal shore, wetlands, and the exact 1900 shoreline have not been reconstructed.

properties.name: Lac Mai-Ndombe
properties.attribution: HydroLAKES v1.0, Messager et al. (2016), CC BY 4.0. Geometry simplified to 35 m before conversion to WGS84.
properties.historical_record: Stanley mapped Lac Leopold II, now Mai-Ndombe, in the 1880s. The Royal Museum account records additional surveys in 1885 and 1886.
properties.geometry_epoch: Modern HydroLAKES open water reference. Seasonal shore, wetlands, and the exact 1900 shoreline have not been reconstructed.

properties.name: Lake Wakatipu
properties.attribution: HydroLAKES (Messager et al. 2016), HydroSHEDS; selected feature geometry exported in WGS84
properties.geometry_epoch: modern HydroLAKES open-water reference for a lake documented before 1900
properties.historical_evidence_note: Te Huruhuru drew Whakatipu Waimāori for Edward Shortland in 1844 (Alexander Turnbull Library E-333-035); James Hector's 1863 report records his field visit. Heritage New Zealand dates construction of the Kawarau Falls outlet gates to 1924. Otago Regional Council reports these gold-mining gates are not in use and the lake level is essentially natural. SWBD gives a modern open-water reference. The exact circa-1900 shoreline and flood levels have not been reconstructed.
